# `packages/AppCompiler.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/packages/AppCompiler.js`

AppCompiler.js — compile an ingested source bundle into a signed `.prpkg`. Two paths: 1. NATIVE — the folder already has a valid `manifest.json` + JS entry. Files are packaged as-is under `files/`. 2. AUTO   — any HTML/WebGPU app. We probe it (engine/compat), generate a compatibility profile, an embedded source module (`__compat_source.js`), and a bootloader entry (`index.js`) that calls `engine.compat.boot(...)` at mount time. A normal WebGPU app → an engine-native, signed OS app. Output uses PackageBuilder.buildV2 (signed + encrypted + merkle + cert). With a developer (self-signed) key the package verifies as the community/unofficial tier; a root-issued cert promotes it to trusted.

| `_compatGuestClass` | `static _compatGuestClass()` | The shared CompatGuestApp bootloader class body. Identical text is emitted by PackageLoader's self-heal path so old and new packages behave the same. Beyond booting the guest, the bootloader INJECTS lifecycle commands into the OS CommandBus at mount (capability-gated via `cmd.register`) and tears them down on unmount — the build-time "command injection" + interception seam. |
| `_genSourceModule` | `static _genSourceModule(files, entry, profile)` | Embed the guest files + profile as `files/__compat_source.js`. |

## Notes & Examples

### Packaging & trust tiers

OS apps ship as signed `.prpkg` bundles (V2: signed + encrypted + merkle + cert). A developer (self-signed) key verifies as the **community / unofficial** tier; a root-issued cert promotes it to **trusted**, and capability grants scale with the tier.

**See also:** [Security & Trust Model](/concepts/security-model.md) · [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md)

### Packaging & trust tiers

OS apps ship as signed `.prpkg` bundles (V2: signed + encrypted + merkle + cert). A developer (self-signed) key verifies as the **community / unofficial** tier; a root-issued cert promotes it to **trusted**, and capability grants scale with the tier.

**Example: Loading a package with trust check**
```js
import { PackageLoader } from 'webgpu-os/packages/PackageLoader.js';

const pkg = await PackageLoader.load('./my-app.prpkg', {
  requiredTier: 'community',  // or 'trusted' for stricter caps
  capabilities: ['storage', 'network']
});

// Trust tier determines what APIs are available
if (pkg.trustTier === 'trusted') {
  pkg.grantCapability('raw-gpu');
}
```

**See also:** [Security & Trust Model](/concepts/security-model.md) · [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md)

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
